result.summary: Checks 1, 3, 4, 5 PASS; checks 2 and 6 surface two genuine, independently-verified defects -- FAILing per this gate's no-partial-credit rule. (1) PASS: this branch now has REQ-206 merged as an ancestor (git log main shows 2d068c79 'REQ-206: SwiftRoute scenario execution (S7 simulation harness) (#767)'; test/support/simulation/{runner.ex,scenario_fixture.ex} exist on this branch). Read runner.ex directly: line 45 `required(:via) => :api | :gui | :skip`, line 107/197 `disposition: :executed | :unbuilt_feature`, lines 314-327 the `:skip` step-execution clause -- REQ-206's vocabulary extension is real and matches what design section 0.1 assumed. Read scenario_fixture.ex: line 40-41 `@spec load!(path :: String.t()) :: Scenario.t()` / `def load!(path) do` -- the function the design imports and calls (never re-implements) genuinely exists. Design's OQ-1 fallback branch is therefore not needed (see defect 2 below on why the doc must still say so). (3) PASS: grepped test/support/simulation/ and lib/letflow/ for `audit_event_ordering` -- the ONLY hits are inside the design doc itself; it is genuinely new, not already shipped by REQ-205/206. Its spec (section 3.2) is signature/type-shape/prose only (`Scenario.expected_outcome().verification.method :: ... | :audit_event_ordering`, an `args` map shape, and a prose description of verify_outcome/2's new clause) -- no function body. (4) PASS: grepped every code fence in the doc (19 fences) for `defmodule`/`defstruct`/`def `/`def(` -- zero matches anywhere in the document. The two map-literal fences (report entry at lines 624-637, section 6's YAML report) are data shapes, not implementation; the test-module-structure fence (lines 666-687) is a prose skeleton (`test "..." -- <description>`), not real ExUnit code. (5) PASS: section 8's table maps all 6 of docs/requirements.yaml's real REQ-207 acceptance_criteria (verified by reading the live yaml entries at lines 11773-11779) to concrete design sections -- no TBD, no criterion left unmapped. DEFECT A (blocks check 2): section 4.1 step 2 specifies `grep -c "title:.*[Ee]ntit" docs/requirements.yaml` and states 'confirm this returns 0'. Independently ran this exact command: it returns 7, not 0 -- `grep -n "title:.*[Ee]ntit" docs/requirements.yaml` shows all 7 matches are false positives from the substring "entit" occurring inside "identity" (6 unrelated identity-subsystem requirement titles at lines 789/3446/4120/4158/4192/4240) plus REQ-207's own title (line 11715, self-referential, not a claim by another requirement). The underlying conclusion (no requirement claims the entity/entity-query subsystem) is still correct -- section 0.5's broader, manually-filtered `grep -n -i "entit"` pass got this right -- but section 4.1 is explicitly documented as 'a concrete, re-runnable procedure' that ELIXIR-DEV must re-run at implementation time without re-deriving from this design doc's prior finding. As specified, a literal re-run returns nonzero, which per section 4.1's own branching logic ('If this ever returns nonzero, name the specific REQ-NNN id and check its status field') forces the re-verifier to pick one of 7 unrelated identity-titled requirements and misreport it as an in-flight claimant of the entity/entity-query subsystem in the BLOCKED_ON_DEPENDENCY report -- exactly the kind of implementation-time ambiguity this gate exists to catch before it reaches ELIXIR-DEV. The same wrong claim ("grep -c ... == 0") is also baked into section 4.3's hand-built report-entry evidence text (line 631), so it isn't an isolated typo -- it propagates into the artifact ELIXIR-DEV would ship. Section 4.1's grep needs a word-bounded pattern that does not match "identity" (e.g. requiring the literal word "entity"/"entities", not any occurrence of the substring "entit") before this design is re-verifiable as claimed. DEFECT B (blocks check 6): section 7's OQ-1 is still framed as an open, unresolved question -- 'whether REQ-206 has merged to main by the time REQ-207's Step 2a begins... ELIXIR-DEV must check git log main --oneline | grep -i REQ206 ... before starting, not assume either way.' Independently confirmed this session: REQ-206 HAS merged to main (commit 2d068c79, ancestor of this branch, confirmed above under check 1) -- the merge happened after this design session authored section 0.1's 'not yet merged' finding (this branch's own git log shows the design-session commit a1418158 'step-01 PASS -- defer step-02a pending REQ-206 merge' predates 2d068c79). This project's own established standard -- cited explicitly in this gate's brief, and the precedent is REQ-206's own OQ-1/1b/2/3 rework -- prohibits silently leaving open a question that is now resolvable from material already available in this same session (a single `git log` call, which I ran, settles it). The design doc must be updated to state OQ-1 is now RESOLVED/MOOT (REQ-206 has merged; ScenarioFixture.load!/1 and the :skip/:unbuilt_feature vocabulary are confirmed present on this branch per check 1 above; section 0.1's fallback-plan branch is not exercised), not left as a live open question for ELIXIR-DEV to re-derive from scratch.

issues.title: Section 4.1's AC4 re-verification grep is unreliable -- false-positives on "identity", contradicting its own stated 0 result
issues.detail: `grep -c "title:.*[Ee]ntit" docs/requirements.yaml` returns 7 today, not the 0 that section 4.1 (and section 4.3's evidence bullet, line 631) states it should return. All 7 matches are substring collisions with "identity" (6 unrelated requirement titles) plus REQ-207's own self-referential title -- none names an entity/entity-query subsystem requirement, so the underlying BLOCKED_ON_DEPENDENCY conclusion is still correct, but the exact command specified as the re-runnable check is not fit for purpose: a literal re-run at implementation time returns nonzero and, per section 4.1's own branching logic, would force naming one of the 7 unrelated identity-titled requirements as an in-flight claimant. Fix: use a word-bounded pattern that matches only the literal word "entity"/"entities" (not any substring occurrence of "entit"), re-verify it returns 0 against the live docs/requirements.yaml, and update section 4.3's evidence bullet text to match.
